timeline.description: Machine learning model screened 12,000+ Li-containing materials down to 317 candidates, then to 21 predicted fast conductors.

_llm_flag.reasoning: The paper explicitly states the screening workflow: (1) “screened all 12 000+ Li-containing materials” (Page 2) and this “identifies 317 materials” (Page 2). (2) It then states: “Screening this list of 317 candidate materials identifies 21 crystalline compounds that are predicted to be fast ion conductors...” (Page 2). This matches the extracted timeline statement (12,000+ → 317 → 21 predicted fast conductors).

timeline.description: DFT-MD simulations (400-1200 K, tens to hundreds of ps) performed on ML-selected and randomly selected materials to compute Li diffusivity and extrapolate RT ionic conductivity.

_llm_flag.reasoning: The paper supports that DFT-MD simulations were run at elevated temperatures (initially 900 K, with additional/alternate temperatures; explicit examples include 400 K, 500 K, 700 K, 900 K, 1100 K, and 1200 K) for tens to hundreds of picoseconds, on both ML-selected and randomly selected materials, to compute Li diffusivity and then extrapolate room-temperature ionic conductivity via a 2–3 point Arrhenius extrapolation (Figure 1; Section II; Tables 1–2). However, the extracted temperature range '400–1200 K' is not stated as a defined workflow range in the narrative; the workflow text emphasizes 'initially 900 K' plus lower temperatures if melting and alternate temperatures if diffusion is observed, rather than a declared 400–1200 K range. Also, the workflow computes ionic conductivity (via diffusivity + Einstein relation) and extrapolates to RT conductivity; it does not say they extrapolate RT conductivity specifically from 'Li diffusivity' alone (they use diffusivity to get conductivity then extrapolate).
_llm_flag.suggested_fix: DFT-MD simulations were performed on ML-selected and randomly selected materials, initially at 900 K (~50–100 ps; tens to hundreds of ps total). If Li diffusion was observed, simulations were repeated at 1–2 alternate temperatures (and restarted at lower T if melting occurred) to compute Li diffusivity/ionic conductivity and make a 2–3 point Arrhenius extrapolation to room-temperature ionic conductivity.
